motivation: The preregistered one-year positive sea-ice-duration mechanism was not supported despite a 96.4% common long-term abundance component. Test a predeclared low-frequency mechanism without tuning the smoothing window on outcomes.

predictor.definition: mean SIDuration over annual transition years t-K+1 through t
predictor.direction: longer low-frequency sea-ice duration predicts less-negative K-year population growth
predictor.source: same frozen EDI/mirror source as PALMER_SEAICE_HABITAT_MECHANISM_V1

models.T1: G5 ~ centered interval-midpoint year + z(trailing-5-year mean SIDuration)

validation.purge_rule: For held-out interval [t-5,t], exclude every training window sharing any census endpoint or annual transition year with that interval.
validation.decision: support only if primary gain > 0 and full-data sea-ice coefficient > 0

robustness: repeat the same predeclared procedure at K=3
repeat the same predeclared procedure at K=7
repeat K=5 after excluding Litchfield from the summed population
diagnostics: report correlation between midpoint year and trailing sea ice to expose trend collinearity
report non-overlapping phase-specific sea-ice coefficients for K=5
report number of training windows per purged fold
interpretation_boundaries: This is a new post-negative hypothesis, not an independent preregistration.
A positive result would support timescale separation, not prove sea ice is causal.
A nonpositive incremental gain over time trend would reject the simple low-frequency sea-ice explanation.
Do not tune K after seeing results; K=5 is primary and K=3/7 are fixed robustness checks.
next_gate: Only after freezing this result may additional sea-ice phenology variables, prey mediators, or terrestrial weather mechanisms be opened.
